reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-30 feet on minnows and jigs over trees.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Conditions at Lake Amistad continue to transition into a classic spring bass pattern, with water temperatures ranging from the high 50s to mid 60s. Many buck bass and some females are moving shallow into spawning areas, and bass are being caught in 0-10 feet of water. With a warming trend in the long-range forecast, bass fishing should remain strong over the next 8-12 weeks as fish progress from pre-spawn to spawn and post-spawn in shallow areas–making it an excellent time to be on the lake. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Aquilla fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 10-12 feet of water on minnows and jigs. Bass are fair on spinnerbaits in 10-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Prespawn bass are feeding heavily. Colder days seem to have bass relating to deep water while warmer days have fish moving shallower for the impending spawn. Crappie and white bass are being caught up the creeks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in pre-spawn mode with a decent concentration of fish roaming and on the deeper grass .As for the shallow bite some of the fish in the deeper grass will start moving up in the afternoons as water temps peak. Crappie are schooled up roaming out in the main lake areas and some still on brush piles.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: An early week small cold front pushed the bass to deep drop-offs near spawning areas. Lake Austin has been producing good bass in the hydrilla. The bass spawn is well underway, with many bass positioned shallow and actively on beds. A consistent pattern has been fishing inside grass lines with drop-shot rigged finesse worms in less than 6 feet of water where bass are staging and guarding spawning areas. Large schools of bass are also roaming open water chasing shad and can be targeted with forward-facing sonar and weightless soft plastic jerkbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be on spawning beds, target these areas with bladed jigs, rattletraps or spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good next to timber on minnows in 20-30 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs or minnows in the mouths of coves and river channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is slow, then improves after a few hours. Crappie are slow as fish transition to the mouths of coves and river channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Crappie should be transitioning towards coves. Bass should be in a pre-spawn with fish shallow on beds or staging on points to move shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Some black bass are being caught around weeds in 3-5 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in a prespawn and this next wave of warm weather should trigger the first spawn. Male crappie are shallow and in the creeks. Crappie bite is fair with jigs or minnows on docks in 15-30 feet of water with some roaming in 20-30 feet. Male 1-3 pound bass have pushed shallow, with big bass still in 10-20 feet. Largemouth bass are fair with Alabama rigs on main lake points, creek channels, or on banks in the late afternoons. Bass will be pushing shallower with this warm weather. Hybrids are fair deadsticking slabs and flukes on main lake humps and points. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.23 pounds are excellent on soft plastic finesse lure in Lone Star Disco color scoping around docks and jigs in 10-12 feet, or jerkbaits in 3-8 feet on the rocks around main lake pockets and points. Crappie are fair to 10 inches on minnows in the main lake scattered brush piles and on docks 15-18 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 10-15 feet of water on brush with chartreuse jigs or minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Several nice size bass were caught during this last New Moon. Over the last week one bass weighed in at 12 pound bass, two bass over 10 pounds and four bass over 9 pounds. Crappie are good.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper and black bass activity remains slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have definitely started to spawn.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing is excellent for channel catfish and blue catfish, as well as some white bass and black bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass action is improving quickly, with buck bass fanning beds and larger females moving in behind them; with shad pushing shallow, rattle traps and perch-colored baits are getting strong reaction strikes in skinny water. Crappie are moving shallow on the north end with warming water, while on the south end they remain on structure in 13-24 feet but are beginning to transition; minnows and jigs are working lake-wide. Hybrid stripers are being caught in 8-28 feet on slabs, spoons, and large minnows or shad, though many are juveniles–check identification using Texas Parks and Wildlife Department guidance or the Outdoor Annual app.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on jigs or minnows in the mouths of coves and river channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Bass fair for fish up to 2 pounds on plastics. No signs of spawning bass. Crappie fair on jigs but better on minnows.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving into a pre-spawn pattern into boat docks and slips. Black bass should be staging on spawning beds in shallow water.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning in less than 5 feet of water. Bass are feeding on the recent shad hatch.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: The morning bass bite is slow and improves when the temperature warms midday. There were some shallow crappie before this last cold blast pushed them back to deeper water. The lake is super healthy and loaded with crappie and bait. Lots of black crappie still on bridges before they make a major move shallow. Most crappie baits will work this time of year if you are fishing where they are.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on deep structure with minnows and jigs. Crappie should spawn by the end of March, if the weather stays warm. Reports of a 14 pound bass. Target bass on the points with red crankbait or lipless crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass continue to transition shallow towards pre-spawn areas. Bass continue to be slow after the recent cold front, but action should improve as warming trends hold. Bass are also feeding on shad near main lake points, especially during the middle of the day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Lake Granbury crappie bite is good to excellent on many areas of the lake. Largemouth bass up to 8 pounds are fair to good working soft plastics near creek entrances and in the back of creeks on those warmer afternoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 7 pounds on jigs and worms fished up river around cover. Crappie are fair on minnows fished up river at night and on jigs fished in shallow water in the backs of sloughs and ditches.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are being caught in 2-4 feet of water under dead lily pads and around cypress trees near adjacent drop-offs, with spinnerbaits, buzzbaits, and chatterbaits in white and green producing strong results. Crappie are holding tight to structure in the muddy East Fork and Lucious Bayou and are biting hand-tied jigs and small dark plastics.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in a mix of late pre-spawn and early spawning phases, though reduced water clarity has made sight-fishing more challenging. Most bites are coming from less than 15 feet of water as bass continue transitioning shallow. Bass are good in 8-15 feet of water with deep diving jerkbaits around submerged trees or rockpiles was very productive.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in shallow water on bladed jigs or rattletraps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Prespawn bass are feeding heavily. Colder days seem to have bass relating to deep water while warmer days have fish moving shallower for the impending spawn. Crappie and white bass are being caught up the creeks. Bass fishing is picking up, water temperatures are starting to rise back up to what they should be this time of the year.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with fish hanging out in flats and at the mouths of coves. Black crappie fishing is good as fish move into creek channels north of the 155 bridge to stage for the upcoming spawn. White crappie are holding on timber and transitioning toward shallower areas as they prepare to spawn. Bass are transitioning to 3-6 feet of water on bladed jigs, rattletraps and Texas rigged senkos.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15 feet of water on brush with jigs. Male crappie are on spawning nests. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are in all stages of the spawns. Spawning bass can be caught with weightless plastics up shallow.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow to fair in 15-38 feet of water with minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing continues to be excellent for crappie, largemouth bass and white bass. Crappie are starting to load up on the Lake Limestone Marina and campground pier. Largemouth bass will move to 5 feet or less to spawning beds on Texas rigs, spinnerbaits, and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Black bass activity is fair, with fish holding on points, timber, and creek mouths; slow-rolled spinnerbaits, soft plastics, and crankbaits are producing the best results.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15 feet of water on brush with jigs. Male crappie are on spawning nests. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are excellent with bladed jigs and wacky worms in the hydrilla. Crappie are excellent with minnows in brush piles from 12-20 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: The water temperature rose significantly bringing some bass to spawning beds a few weeks earlier than normal. Largemouth bass are excellent in shallow water with a bladed jig, or large swimbaits. Crappie are fair on small 1/16 ounce white and chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Crappie populations remain good, while catfish action is slow.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases and laydowns in 1-3 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Bass are transitioning into spawning areas. Crappie are fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair to good in the staging zone just outside shallow water or on brush piles with blue jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good for catches up to 6 pounds, a few up to 9 pounds, and one over 13 pounds. Crappie fishing is starting to improve in 20-30 feet of water with fish suspended 10 feet into the treetops.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and bass are good with fish spawning along the banks. Crappie are good on minnows or jigs. Bass are biting rattletraps and spoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Smaller crappie can be caught in the shallows, with larger catches still in deeper water. As the water continues to warm, crappie will move to the banks to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: The water temperature rose significantly bringing some bass to spawning beds a few weeks earlier than normal. Largemouth bass are excellent in shallow water with a bladed jig, or large swimbaits. Crappie are fair on clear crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Bass have started to move up shallow in 10 feet or less water using crankbaits and swimbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on ledges in about 12-18 feet. Bass moved to ledges around 15 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Locate schools of bait and target those areas with the 2-3 jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Crappie are fair and also moving out from brush and out of deeper water along flats and levees moving into feeder creeks on the warm sunny days.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Some crappie are starting to spawn. Crappie are good in 12-15 feet of water near spawning flats with jigs or minnows. Bass are staging to spawn in 5-12 feet of water. Sand bass are beneath the birds with live bait or deadsticking slabs. Blue catfish and crappie are mixed in. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass will continue to make their way to the spawning coves as long as the warming trend continues.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Focus on points and pockets where bass are staging and preparing to transition shallow.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina the crappie bite is good, and catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. Crappie are good with fish scattered on the main lake brush in 8-16 feet of water with chartreuse and white or shad color jigs and minnows. Black bass are staging for the spring spawn.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Spence fishing report
reports.text: No signs or reports of crappie.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and bass are in a prespawn and the spawn should fire up any day. Crappie are good at the crappie house and concrete structures with jigs and minnows. Bass are fair with red crankbaits or lipless crankbaits in 5-8 feet of water on points, or on steep rocky banks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: Crappie anglers are getting out on the water, but the bite remains slow as temperatures are still on the cool side.
reports.by: Chad Kinsfather, Lavaca Navidad River Authority

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been holding on structure and ledges in 20-25 feet of water, but be looking for them to be on the move to shallower water as the warm weather continues this week.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with a 4 inch swimbait rigged on a keel weighted hook fished around shallow submerged brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the creeks and rivers gearing up for the spawn.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in shallow water with minnows or jigs. Bass are good in shallow water with rattletraps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent while fish are in prespawn patterns staging on brush and structure in 15-18 feet of water along the edges of creek channels. Female crappies are full of eggs. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with fish holding on shallow structure near spawning grounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be staging on spawning beds, or on points nearing spawning grounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 15 feet of water moving up the creeks and rivers. Largemouth bass are fair using crankbaits on windy bank lines.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good using spinnerbaits up against the cattails. Crappie are good in shallow timber using jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good as fish start to pull off of main channels and move into staging areas to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: There have been no recent reports on crappie or catfish. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Aquilla fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 10-12 feet of water with minnows or jigs. Bass are fair on spinnerbaits in 10-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with fish staging to spawn around shallow cover. Bass can be caught on weightless senkos, with crankbaits and spinnerbaits in shallow water, and with Alabama rigs and jigs in deeper water. Crappie should be feeding heavily on shad prespawn as well.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Offshore bass can be found with livescope then have an umbrella rig and a minnow on a jig head ready to go. Crappie are schooled up roaming out in the main lake areas and some still on brush piles.
reports.by: Captain Kirk Pasalich, Artifishable Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are moving to shallow water this week due to the warming trend. Be on the look out for bedding bass in the creek and around inner grass lines.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in a prespawn pattern moving towards spawning grounds in the river channels near the 21 Bridge. Crappie are slow with the best bite on jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Morning bass action is improving, but the best bite continues to be mid morning to afternoon. Crappie are slow with fish clinging to the bottom.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Shallow bass can be caught with rattle traps, and some deeper bass can be caught on Carolina rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is fair with jigs or minnows on docks in 15-30 feet of water with some roaming in 20-30 feet. Largemouth bass are fair with Alabama rigs on main lake points, creek channels, or on banks in the late afternoons. Bass will be pushing shallower with this warm weather. Hybrids are fair deadsticking slabs and flukes on main lake humps and points. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.19 pounds are excellent on soft plastic creature baits in Lone Star Disco scoping around docks and jigs in 10-12 feet, and jerkbaits in 3-8 feet of water on the rocks around main lake pockets and points. Crappie are slow to 10 inches on minnows in the main lake scattered brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 10-15 feet of water on brush with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: The bass spawn has started with the new moon, so expect big females to be caught on wacky worms, Texas senkos, chatterbaits, swimbaits, swim jigs and topwater frogs.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper and black bass fishing remain slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite is improving with fish moving shallow due to the warmer water temperatures. Bass are in a pre-spawn and some are spawning throughout the lake. Bass are grouped, so if you catch one do not be scared to stick around for a while. Bass are good on the outside grass lines of main lake points with a neko rig and a dropshot.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite continues to improve. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 7-12 feet of water around bridge pylons, brush piles, and docks. Guides report improving conditions, with larger crappie showing up more consistently.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing is excellent, with plenty of channel and blue catfish being caught and some black bass also taken from shore.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Limits of channel catfish and largemouth bass are common.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Buck bass are stacked in the grass fanning beds and acting territorial, with some larger females easing in behind them; with shad thick in the shallows, rattle traps and swimbaits that mimic nervous baitfish are getting hammered. Crappie are beginning to move shallow up north with warmer water, though some remain on structure in 3-20 feet, while down south they’re still holding deeper on 12-25 foot structure but starting to transition; minnows and jigs are working across all areas. Hybrid stripers are being caught in 10-26 feet on slabs, spoons, large minnows, and shad, with many juveniles mixed in among schooling whites or moving shallower–check the tooth patch for identification via Texas…
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent on minnows. Bass are fair on minnows and plastics. Mostly juvenile catches, with some 2-3 pound bass are being reported.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in the boat slips. Black bass are slow.
reports.by: Captain Bobby Mann, Catch a Dream Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with Carolina rigs in 5-9 feet of water, or squarebill crankbaits over the grass. Bass are in prespawn, with the first spawn push complete. Many small bass are running the banks biting rattle traps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Lake Fork crappie fishing has seen major changes and moves. We are seeing good amounts of black crappie stopping on bridges as they make these moves. Timber and flats close to spawning areas in 12-22 feet are seeing white crappie also beginning to appear. We should see the crappie fishing get better and better as the water warms more.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are beginning to move up into shallow water as they transition toward prespawn areas. Bass are slow, but action should continue to improve as warming trends hold. Bass are also feeding on shad near main lake points, especially during the middle of the day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 12-14 feet deep in brush with jigs. Bass are slow on main lake points with slow moving baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Best fishing reports on Granbury are for crappie and catfish. Crappie limits are being taken on the upper portions of the lake. Largemouth bass are fair to good on soft plastics worked near deeper docks and structure with some fish near laydowns in the river above Granbury.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on jigs and rattle traps fished up river around timber. Crappie are showing up in shallow sloughs and coves off the river with night fishing producing best.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Fishing on Lake Houston is excellent overall, led by outstanding largemouth bass action–recent tournament results topped 22 pounds for five fish, reflecting strong populations. Bass are aggressively striking crankbaits, spinnerbaits, and especially chatterbaits, with white skirts and green paddle tails producing best around drop-offs, docks, back lakes, and cypress trees in 4-6 feet. Crappie are abundant in Lucious Bayou and the East Fork, holding tight to structure despite slightly off-colored water; live minnows, small hand-tied jigs, and plastics are all effective.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are moving shallow, and can be caught on the bank and around docks with jigs, chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, and rattle traps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with fish staging to spawn around shallow cover. Bass can be caught on weightless senkos, with crankbaits and spinnerbaits in shallow water, and with Alabama rigs and jigs in deeper water. Crappie should be feeding heavily on shad prespawn as well. Bass fishing is picking up, water temperatures are starting to rise back up to what they should be this time of the year.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good at the mouth of coves on timber. Black crappie fishing is good as fish move into creek channels north of the 155 bridge to stage for the upcoming spawn. White crappie are holding on timber and transitioning toward shallower areas as they prepare to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Then switch to slabs or vertical jigging when fish are holding in one area. Crappie are fair with many roaming north from the dam area, and scattered in shallow water away from the dam. Largemouth bass are fair with fewer suspended fish reported recently.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20 feet of water on brush with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass fishing is picking up as the water temperature rises. Bass are good slowly dragging a Texas rig over shallow rock piles and rocky banks.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing is excellent for crappie, largemouth bass and white bass. Numbers of crappie are being caught at the lake Limestone Marina and campground ground as well. Largemouth bass will move to 5 feet or less to spawning beds on Texas rigs, spinnerbaits, and chatterbaits.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair on soft plastics, spinnerbaits, and crankbaits worked around timber, drop-offs, and creek edges in 4-12 feet. White bass are staging up the river and in creek channels, hitting jigs, slabs, and minnows. Crappie action is still slow overall with scattered fish on deeper brush piles and structure in 12-20 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 20 feet of water on brush with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good along the inside edge of the hydrilla with swimbaits and wacky worms. Crappie are good in brush piles in 15-25 feet with minnows.
reports.by: Hambone fishing Reported by Hambone fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Water stained; 37 degrees; 43.03 feet below pool.Largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, and sand bass all have continued to flourish around many parts of the lake. Crappie have been slow again this week.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Murvaul fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair on bladed jigs and shallow diving crankbaits in shallow water. Crappie are good on docks and shallow stumps with chartreuse and black jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: The water temperature rose significantly bringing some bass to spawning beds a few weeks early than normal. Largemouth bass are excellent in shallow water with a bladed jig, or large swimbaits. Crappie are fair on small 1/16 ounce white and chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Larger female bass should be feeding heavily as they build up before the spawn. The crappie population remains strong, while catfish activity has been slow. The water temperature rose significantly bringing some bass to spawning beds a few weeks early than normal. Largemouth bass are excellent in shallow water with a bladed jig, or large swimbaits. Crappie are fair on small 1/16 ounce white and chartreuse jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases and laydowns in 1-3 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Bass are beginning to transition into spawning areas with the warmer weather we have had lately. Crappie are fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in shallow water or on brush piles with blue jigs or minnows. White bass are mixed in with the crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good for catches up to 9 pounds, and few reported over 10 pounds. Crappie are good suspended down 25-36 feet in deep trees along river Channel swings.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and bass are good with fish spawning along the banks. Crappie are good on minnows or jigs. biting rattletraps and spoons.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 14 feet of water on minnows and jigs. As the water continues to warm, crappie will move to the banks to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: The water temperature rose significantly bringing some bass to spawning beds a few weeks early than normal. Largemouth bass are excellent in shallow water with a bladed jig, or large swimbaits. Crappie are fair on clear crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Bass have started to move up shallow in 10 feet of water or less water biting crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on ledges in about 12-18 feet. Bass have moved to ledges around 15 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with fish in a prespawn. Bass may be in 6-12 feet of water weedlines near secondary points. It is nearing spawning time for bass. Sand bass are beneath the birds with live bait or deadsticking slabs. Blue catfish and crappie are mixed in. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black Bass will move to spawning coves as the water warms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and white bass remain up the river, where minnows and Road Runners are producing.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good at the crappie house and concrete structures with jigs and minnows. Catfish are mixed under the crappie. Bass are fair with red crankbaits or lipless crankbaits in 5-8 feet of water on points, or on steep rocky banks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair targeting nomadic fish roaming in open water with minnow-style soft plastics. Large groups of bass, sometimes numbering dozens of fish, are following bait and can provide fast action once located. Alabama rigs will catch fish in submerged vegetation in 12–20 feet of water, where anglers can often catch multiple bass from the same area.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Swimbaits and slabs are working best in 10-30 feet. Crappie have been decent on the 2 mile bridge in 15-20 feet on jigs. The largemouth bite has been better than average over the last two weeks.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texana fishing report
reports.text: There are still no signs of crappie, though a few bass are being caught north of 59 by small boats able to launch.
reports.by: Chad Kinsfather, Lavaca Navidad River Authority

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving up near creeks and on structures in 10-15 feet of water. Bass are moving to spawning areas and gorging on the large amount of bait in the lake.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Crappie action is also good in the backs of creeks; although some areas were muddied by last weekend’s rain, most are clearing quickly, and both live bait and jigs are producing in 4-10 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in shallow water with minnows or jigs. Bass are slow in 6-8 feet of water and in deep water with crankbaits, or finesse worms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving up the creeks and rivers and are being caught in about 15 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using crankbaits on windy bank lines.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good, slowly bouncing jigs off the bottom. Crappie are good under bridge pylons with jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing remains challenging overall, though quality fish are being caught at times, with the most consistent bites coming off the tops of ledges in 15-20 feet of water near steep drop-offs, as well as in remaining grass beds in pockets with gradually tapering depths. Crappie reports have been limited over the past couple of weeks. Report by Kurt Dove, Amistad Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Aquilla fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 25-30 feet of water with minnows or jigs. Bass are fair on spinnerbaits in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good as fish move shallower and feed heavily. Crappie are loading up around docks getting ready to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is quickly heating up on Lake Austin. Starting to see bass cruising in shallow water, but not quite on spawning beds yet. Bass are good just outside spawning areas with a wacky worm, dropshot, and smaller Texas rigs. Bass are fair on suspending jerkbaits fished over submerged vegetation and mid-strolling minnow-style soft plastics targeting suspended, nomadic fish following baitfish. Bass relating to grass are being caught in 12–20 feet of water, while roaming fish can be found over a variety of depths. Fish are grouped up in areas, and anglers can often catch multiple bass once productive zones are located. Some very large bass have recently been caught, likely representing…

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Work a white 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab with a stinger hook vertically, using a snap-jigging method or a slow-smoking method. Largemouth bass bycatch is beginning to decrease.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow with the best bite on jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow with fish clinging to the bottom.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Water stained; 72 degrees; Fishing has been slow across the board, with redfish, black bass, catfish, and stripers all seeing limited activity.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on docks 15-30 feet deep with some roaming in 20-30 feet. Largemouth bass are fair using Alabama rigs on main lake points, creek channels, or on banks in the late afternoons. Bass will be pushing shallower with this warm weather. White bass and hybrids are fair on main lake humps and points, deadsticking slabs and flukes. Report by Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service.
reports.by: Jack Pellegrini, Lake Bridgeport Crappie Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 9.05 pounds are excellent on soft plastic Prickly Pears in Lone Star Disco scoping around docks and jigs in 10-12 feet of water. Crappie are slow to 11 inches on minnows in main lake scattered brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught on senkos, flukes, chatterbaits, swim jigs and swimbaits. Crappie will be moving up around the trees in 3 feet of water on the main lake soon.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper fishing has been slow, and black bass are sluggish as well.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: The largemouth fishing has improved, fish seem to still be holding out a little deeper. Bass are good on the outside grass lines of main lake points with a neko rig and a dropshot.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Cedar Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite continues to improve. Target crappie with small jigs and minnows in 14-22 feet of water around bridge pylons, brush piles, and docks. Guides report improving conditions, with larger crappie showing up more consistently.
reports.by: Brent Herbeck, Herbeck’s Lonestar Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Some black bass are also being caught off the bank, along with white bass and a few crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Target bass on the points with red crankbait or lipless crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to produce numbers of largemouth bass and channel catfish. Largemouth bass are good on a variety of baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing shows a split pattern, with some fish holding deep and feeding on shad–responding to deep-diving crankbaits and jerkbaits–while others are moving shallow with early bedding activity beginning. Crappie fishing has been good when schools can be located, though weather swings have them moving; the north end is producing limits in 3-8 feet on jigs and minnows, while the south end bite is more inconsistent in 12-34 feet. Hybrid stripers are still being caught dead-sticking in 22-44 feet, though that pattern may fade as temperatures rise; slabs, spoons, and large minnows or shad are also working, with many juvenile hybrids mixed in with white bass, so check identification features if…
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie slow and vertically jigging will be the best tactic. Look in river channels further from the dam for crappie staging in spawning grounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent as fish migrate shallow to spawning grounds.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has turned on this week. Bass are good for quality size fish up to 7 pounds and quantities of fish being caught on soft plastics and crankbaits. Crappie are good on mainly minnows and a few on jigs.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in a prespawn mode. Many small bass are running the banks biting rattle traps. Bass are good in 6-9 feet of water with Carolina rigs. A few small bass caught along the bank with a wacky rig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are stacked up on deep timber along the main lake creek channels like they have been all winter.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 12-20 feet of water on structure with minnows and jigs. Reports of a 14 pound bass. Target bass on the points with red crankbait or lipless crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Fishing remains slow, but bass are beginning to transition toward prespawn locations. Several bass were marked on sonar in 8–10 feet of water, holding tight to structure.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good near deeper docks and creek channel entrances slowly working soft plastics. The best fishing action on Granbury will be crappie.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on jigs and Rattl-traps fished up river around timber. Crappie are showing up in shallow sloughs and coves off the river with night fishing producing best.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving in with the white bass and are being caught on similar lures in the same areas. Largemouth bass fishing continues to improve, with strong tournament weights reflecting a healthy population; anglers are catching them on spinnerbaits, crankbaits, and Texas rigged grubs with 3/16-�¼-ounce weights–heavier if current increases–focusing on secondary drop-offs near docks as well as shallow cypress trees and knees.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Target bass on the points with red crankbait or lipless crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught on crankbaits in 5–12 feet of water around rocky areas and submerged vegetation. Fish are grouped up, and anglers can often catch multiple bass in small productive zones. Bass are holding in shallow to mid-depth areas and appear to be shifting toward pre-spawn patterns.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good as fish move shallower and feed heavily. Crappie are loading up around docks getting ready to spawn. Bass have been found in the 15-20 feet depth range on rock piles, submerged old creek banks, and channel swings.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good at the mouth of coves on timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 25-30 feet of water with chartreuse jigs and minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass fishing is picking up as the water temperature rises. Bass are good slowly dragging a Texas rig over shallow rock piles and rocky banks.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Bass are headed for the banks to get on spawning beds, so it is time for the bank anglers to shine. As far as the lake fishing goes, largemouth bass will move to 5 feet or less on Texas rigs, spinnerbaits, and chatterbaits. Crappie are still deep, but will start trickling into the creeks very soon.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, Lake Limestone Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: White bass remain one of the more reliable targets and can still be found reacting to fast lures when schools are located, while largemouth bass and striped bass will relate to deeper cover and creek channels as they adjust to changing conditions. Catfish are active along main lake channels and creek edges on cut bait or shad, and crappie are fair on minnows and jigs, especially around woody structure and tributary mouths.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with fish in a pre-spawn and spawning in different areas of the lake. Crappie remain good fishing brush piles in 20-25 feet with jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Water stained; 39 degrees; 43.99 feet below pool.Largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, and sand bass all have continued to flourish around many parts of the lake. Crappie have been slow again this week.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Murvaul fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow with medium diving crankbaits and half ounce bladed jigs around main lake points. Crappie are good on chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent on small swimbaits, and Alabama rigs. Crappie are fair on small 1/16 ounce white and chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Larger female bass should be feeding heavily as they build up before the spawn. The crappie population remains strong, while catfish activity has been slow. Largemouth bass are good in shallow water with Carolina rigs or Alabama rigs on main lake points. Crappie are good in schools of 10-20 fish swimming around timber lines. Vertically fish a white and chartreuse crappie jig to fish suspending 10 feet down.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie bite is fair with best bite in the afternoon over morning. Target crappie in shallow water or on brush piles with blue jigs or minnows. Seeing signs of white bass mixed in with crappie, but no schooling action yet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good to 11 pounds with most fish in the 2-4 pounds. Crappie reports are improving. Reports of a limit of crappie in the tops of trees as deep as 50 feet, but primarily in 25-30 feet in the tops of deep trees with minnows working best.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: The bass fishing practically stopped, crappie either retreated to staging areas or never left them. Bass were just about stopped cold, pun intended, but did get somewhat active during the bright, sunny, mild wind days. Crappie, mostly white crappie, continue to be caught primarily deep, around brush and timber 16-22 feet down. Some mixed crappie have been caught around the standard winter bridge and deep end areas, with a lot of juveniles. No male crappie seem to be wearing the tuxedos or blackface yet, but many females are showing the growing eggs.
reports.by: Jim Beggerly, Jim’s Fishing Lake Palestine

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in the creeks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair with white colored bladed jigs or swim jigs around grass lines. Crappie are good on white or chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Proctor fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on ledges in about 12-18 feet. Bass moved to deep ledges.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Raven fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass activity should increase with more sunny, water days as they transition into pre-spawn patterns, moving from deeper water into the shallows to feed in preparation for spawning. Crappie are also becoming more active as temperatures approach the mid-50s, following a similar pre-spawn feeding pattern. Expect crappie to push toward shallower areas of the lake by late February into early March, possibly sooner depending on weather trends and water temperature.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Locate schools of bait and fish those areas with the 2-3 jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Crappie are fair and also moving out from brush and out of deeper water along flats and levees moving into feeder creeks on the warm sunny days.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Black bass can be caught on shallow baits such as square bills and chatterbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and white bass are still holding up the river, with minnows and Road Runners producing the best results.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina the crappie bite is good, and catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. Black bass are starting to stage for spring spawn. Bass are fair on craw jigs and slow moving plastics baits in 6-14 feet of water. On the lake crappie are good with various jigs and minnows holding tight under brush in 8-16 feet of water or roaming.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good at the crappie house and concrete structures with jigs and minnows. Catfish and drum are mixed in with the crappie on the concrete structure. Bass are fair with red crankbait or lipless crankbaits.

reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: With the warmer sunnier days we have had and are forecasted in the coming days the crappie will be moving a little more into the 15-20 feet of water on structures.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Toledo Bend is fishing well, with water temperatures in the mid to upper 50s and bass being caught in a wide range of depths from 2 to 25 feet, giving anglers success with a variety of techniques across the lake. Crappie are beginning to bite well in the backs of creeks, showing up in 2-8 feet of water on live bait and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair being caught mid-strolling minnow-style soft plastics for nomadic fish roaming open water, with forward-facing sonar playing a key role in locating these schools. Large groups of bass, sometimes numbering dozens of fish, are following bait and can provide fast action once located.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 8-12 feet of water on the main lake or in 1-3 feet of water in the creeks with jigs or minnows. Bass are slow in 6-8 feet of water and in deep water with crankbaits, or finesse worms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite is slow while fish are scattered and lethargic. Some crappie are roaming in channels in 30 feet of water. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are schooled up on structure and scattered.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on timber along the main channel, and up the river on structure or roaming.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be fair in 25-35 feet with minnows.
reports.by: Randy Britton, The Bait Shop, Post, Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Aquilla fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on brush piles in 20-30 feet of water with minnows or jigs. Bass are fair on spinnerbaits in 15-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good fishing spinnerbaits and swimbaits over grass flats.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass will be biting at the hot water discharge, or schooled up on deep main lake humps and drop-offs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: These fish are very responsive to snap-jigging with the white, 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab with stinger hook. The trick is adding an intentional pause after the jigging stroke, and making sure the jigging stroke ends with the slab about 6 inches off bottom. Numbers of keeper largemouth bass are falling to this deep, snap-jigging approach as well.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Benbrook fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good next to structure on minnows in 20-30 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been slow due to weather. A few bass can be caught in 6-8 feet of water with Texas rigs or shaky heads around tree lines or calmer banks catching sun. Crappie enter a hibernation state when the water drops into the 40s, so expect the bite to be slow. Crappie will be deep, then suspend higher in the water column on bright and sunny days.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Striper action is slow, black bass are slow, and catfish are slow as well.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8.33 pounds are excellent on soft plastics, in Lone Star Disco color, scoping around docks and stroking them on the ledges in 15-18 feet of water. Crappie are slow to 11 inches on minnows or jigs on main lake scattered brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Continue to target bass on the bottom around deep cover with a jig or a Texas rigged craw or creature bait. If the bass are finicky, downsize to a shaky head or a Ned rig and just let it soak.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with fish bunched up in 25 feet of water on brush and standing timber suspended 25-30 feet down with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been consistent on an Alabama rig with rare bites on chatterbaits and jerkbaits. Bass should start biting rattle traps, jerkbaits, swim jigs, chatterbaits and Alabama rigs.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Striper bite is slow, and black bass action is slow as well.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass fishing has been decent. Bass are positioned on the outside grass edges biting a dropshot or a Texas rig.
reports.by: Tyler Stanley, Game on Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Choke Canyon fishing report
reports.text: Bank fishing has been good, with channel and blue catfish being caught along some bass and white bass from shore.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has also been productive, especially along edges and around large offshore schools of shad. Crappie are being found on structure in 17-25 feet, with minnows and hair jigs outperforming plastics this week; many bites have been very light. Hybrid stripers are active with dead-sticking patterns in the current water temperatures, and anglers are also catching them on slabs, spoons, large minnows, and shad in 25-41 feet.
reports.by: Brad Doyle with Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Dunlap fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on minnows. Bass are slow, with a few reports of single fish catches.
reports.by: Lee Johnson and Kenneth Linder, local anglers

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of small buck bass running the banks. Bass are good in 6-9 feet of water with Carolina rigs. A few small bass caught along the bank with a wacky rig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been slow due to weather conditions. Bass can be caught slowly working Texas rigs and jigs on boat houses with brush. Lake Fork crappie fishing has survived the arctic blast of 2026 without it affecting the bite like it did in 2021 and 2025.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Georgetown fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are slow, and best to target below the thermocline tight to structure fishing slowly with jigs or soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on rock piles in 12-14 feet of water with minnows. Bass are good on main lake points with slow moving baits like jigs and Texas rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Best action continues to be crappie on jigs worked near deeper structure. Largemouth bass continue to be good in numbers with an occasional bigger fish. Look for largemouth near major creek entrances and near deeper docks. Best largemouth presentation is slowly working soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on jigs and black Power Worms. Crappie are starting to show up in shallow sloughs and coves.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell's Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Deadstick small slabs with jigs tied 2 feet above.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O'the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are holding near deep drop-offs and secondary points along main channels, responding to dark Texas-rigged worms, and may move shallow onto flats as the day warms. Crappie has been good in the creeks, Lucious Bayou, and the East Fork, but muddy water will slow the bite; small, dark hand-tied jigs are best when conditions improve.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Inks fishing report
reports.text: Bass are being caught on crankbaits and drop-shot rigged finesse worms fished around rocky areas and submerged vegetation in up to 15 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on chatterbaits, spinnerbaits, and rattle traps out to 8 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Crappie fishing was tough this week, with presentation being key. With warmer weather approaching, expect crappie to begin moving toward spawning areas in the coming weeks. Bass fishing remains good along creek channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 25-30 feet of water with chartreuse jigs and minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are slow but improving on deeper rocky banks.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Anglers are finding white bass schooling in pockets and will often hit spoons or slabs in deeper water, while catfish remain solid along main lake channels and deeper holes on cut bait or live shad. Largemouth bass activity is fair around deeper cover and creek bends on worms, jigs, and plastics, striped bass are fair on spoons or shad offerings, and crappie can be picked up in suitable cover using minnows and small jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Marble Falls fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair in 25-30 feet of water with chartreuse jigs and minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, and sand bass all have continued to flourish around many parts of the lake. Crappie have been slow again this week.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Larger female bass are feeding up ahead of the spawn. Crappie numbers are strong, while catfish activity has been slow.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal's ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nasworthy fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has been fair flipping soft plastics around reed bases and laydowns in 1-5 feet of water. The key is to cover water until you find a good stretch that holds multiple bass. Bass are holding close to heavy cover to stay warm and ambush prey. Crappie were fair around main lake boat docks on chartreuse jigs and catfish were fair on cut bait and stink bait around river channel bends.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair with catches up to 9 pounds possible, but primarily 2-4 pound fish. Crappie are slow, with some action reported near the Lee day area in deep pecan trees on minnows. Slabs and jigging spoons working best.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Hybrids, sand bass and bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Locate schools of bait and fish those areas with the 2-3 jigs tied above a 1 ounce slab. Crappie are fair as fish move from brush to deeper water along flats and levees.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in the creeks, with a better bite bite in 25-40 feet of water on brush and rocks. Dan's Crappie Co.
reports.by: Daniel Koberna, Lt. Dan's Crappie Co

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: This is a great time to Livescope for black bass. The shallow bite for black bass will be tough due the low temperatures.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At the marina the crappie bite is fair, and catfish are fair on minnows or punch bait. Black bass are starting to stage for spring spawn. Bass are fair on craw jigs and slow moving plastics baits in 6-14 feet of water. On the lake crappie are fair with various jigs and minnows holding tight under brush in 8-16 feet of water or roaming.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: These fish are very responsive to snap-jigging with the white, 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab with stinger hook. The trick is adding an intentional pause after the jigging stroke, and making sure the jigging stroke ends with the slab about 6 inches off bottom. Numbers of keeper largemouth bass are falling to this deep, snap-jigging approach as well.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are staying around deeper structures in 20-30 feet of water, with the colder water temps patience is key as they will be moving and feeding a little slower.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Texoma, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Water temperatures are in the mid to low 50s, and bass fishing has been slow due to the colder water. No crappie report at this time.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair to good on jerkbaits fished around windblow points have been working well.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in the creek and river channels. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Welsh fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are stacking up in the brush.
