reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good up in the main lake in brush 30-40 feet of water. White bass are slow on slabs in 30 feet of water. Largemouth bass are fair using soft plastics on deep structure and around docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow on the main lake, but can be caught in creeks and rivers. No report for bass or white bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair over brush in 32-40 feet of water on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on jigs, flatheads good on live bait. Bass are in a prespawn mode with quality fish and limits possible. Bass are best utilizing forward facing sonar using jig head minnow presentations, Texas rigged plastics and jerkbaits. Report by Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide. Bass are slow on Alabama rigs and football jigs near deep water.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow in 5-15 feet of water in grass with Texas rigged worms, wacky rigged senkos and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good fishing small profile Alabama rigs and jerkbaits around suspended fish in deep water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bastrop fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be feeding up in the reeds hitting Texas rigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: For this reason head out rigged with the white 5/8ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are in full pre-spawn mode, and likely begin spawning by the end of the month or beginning of next. Look for black bass suspended in tree lines and around boat houses near the mouths of creeks. Male bass will start cruising the banks preparing nests when the water warms to the upper 50s. Crappie and catfish should be moving shallow when the weather stabilizes, wooly buggers should work well.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: The lake level is low and the bass bite is slow due to the recent cold weather. Look for the bass to head shallow and follow routes to the shallow waters like road beds and timber lines.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass and hybrids are fair on slabs and soft plastics. Crappie are in prespawn mode. Bass are in prespawn mode too.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5 pounds are slow on scope minnows off the rocks, but fair on Hag’s All Around jigs in Juice Box around steep banks and squarebill crankbaits in 2-14 feet of water. Crappie are slow to 1 pound on jigs and minnows in brush piles in 8-12 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has continuously picked up after the latest cold front.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow anywhere near balls of bait. Crappie are good in 10-15 feet of water over brush and trees. Crappie are good in 15-20 feet with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught near trees on senkos and flukes, or in the pad stems around the trees with a swim jig, swimbait, chatterbait or spinnerbait.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Coleman fishing report
reports.text: Target bass with Carolina rigs and football head jigs. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: This warm water power plant lake continues to draw in largemouth bass anglers from all over.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been fair and with the warm up coming they should move back up on the beds. Crappie have been pretty scattered due to the temperature swings. Crappie are being caught in 13-22 feet on or near standing timber and other structures.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cooper fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are starting to migrate in 10-15 feet of water with crappie jigs. Bass are excellent offshore chasing bait balls.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on main lake structure with slabs and in mid depths on chartreuse and white cocahoes. Crappie are fair in open water roaming patterns and in mid depths and main lake structure on jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow with a few catches in 10-20 feet of water. Bass are really good for numbers and size 3-10 feet of water near shallow rock with swimbaits and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow and ready to push to the bank as the weather continues to warm. Bass are good with fish piled up in the trees, and some off points on the edge of coves.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: It has been a cold week with a slow bass bite, but with warmer weather in the forecast expect bass to move shallow and get crazy. Cold water temperatures will slow down the spawn for black bass. Shallow bass will be active on warm sunny days. The crappie should be moving shallow. The Lake Fork crappie bite is really good, if you can stand the cold weather and beat the winds. If you find a crappie and hold an artificial bait above it still enough most fish are crushing that bait.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Target bass with Carolina rigs and football head jigs. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in brush about 15-17 feet deep on jigs and minows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are best on warm days when they move shallow to feed. Soft plastics worked slowly near main lake points will catch largemouth. Crappie are still holding on deeper structure, but will be moving up shortly.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair on white spinnerbaits and red shad power worms. Crappie are good on minnows fished up river at night and in shallow water on slip bobber fished in the backs of coves and ditches.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Deadstick with a slight sway with a slab on stinger hook with a 1/16 ounce jighead 3 inch stick bait with a curly tail 2 feet above.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are just plumb full of eggs and it is time to bust out the crappie gear as crappie will soon be excellent in the shallows. Crappie are in around 8 feet of water very tight to structure. Largemouth bass are starting to spawn in the back lakes and fishing is great!
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Target bass with Carolina rigs and rattle traps. Crappie can be caught with jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Hubbard Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Target bass with Carolina rigs and football head jigs. Crappie can be caught with minnows or jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good using swimbaits for suspended fish, soft plastics on the bank and in brush offshore, or running the banks with rattle traps and chatterbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: The fishing patterns are consistent, but the pattern should as the weather warms Crappie are in 10-20 feet of water on brush piles and deep submerged timber. Crappie are hugging the bottom so you have to let a ⅛ ounce hand tied jig touch the bottom and then slowly lift to entice a bite. Slabs and 3-4 inch flukes have been getting them. Black bass are in 1-5 feet on rocks or concrete, and in 5-10 feet of water shoreline structure. Texas rigs and bass jigs are pulling them out of 15-20 feet deep brush piles. The dam has trees and brush bluegill and crappie are mixed in. Crickets have been king as they also catch a few crappies.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 15-20 feet with chartreuse jigs. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. In the river target bass with a suspended jerkbait, dropshot and Alabama rig between dock, and the big granite boulders. Bass are good near laydowns and brush piles with jigs, Texas rigged soft plastics, lipless crankbaits and square and some days a spinner baits.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass, crappie and white bass are starting to transition to spawning beds. Bass can be caught with Texas rigs and chatterbaits 5 feet or less. Crappie can be caught with minnows in 5 feet or less.
reports.by: Colan Gonzales, CG’s Just Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass should be pushing to spawn on beds, if not on beds they will be on wind blown points.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth and smallmouth bass are fair throughout the lake with silver Kastmasters, and artificial grubs in chartreuse, pearl blue and yellow. Crappie are good with chartreuse jigs and minnows. Don’t forget your slab spoons!
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in shallow grass with a bladed jig, lipless crankbait or chatterbait. Crappie are excellent roaming in standing timber with chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Large numbers and quality size bass can be caught with deep-diving crankbaits, jerkbaits and the Alabama rigs. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are good with dropshot and Carolina rigs in 10 feet of water around grass lines. Crappie are excellent suspended 15-20 feet in timber with a white crappie jig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are moving shallow by docks on jigs, a few fish are roaming the main lake hitting jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 8 pounds on shad patterned jerkbaits or ⅜ inch swimbaits on a umbrella rig on the outside of points or mouths of drains in 12-20 feet of water. Crappie are being caught in the mouth of Elm Creek in deep trees.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Bass and crappie are making a run to the banks. Crappie are good with live minnows or jigs under a slip cork. Some crappie staged in 8-16 feet of water. Bass are good on soft plastics and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow still relating to deeper water. Sand bass and black bass are slow to nonexistent.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on dropshots and medium diving crankbaits in 10-15 feet of water. Crappie are slow, try a clear crappie jig.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 20-34 feet of water with 3/4 ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied 16 inches apart. Small roadrunner type baits and small crappie jigs working. Crappie are fair on minnow with fish relating to brush 18-28 ft deep moving on and off structure and starting to roam the deep flats.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass and small hybrids are scattered, but can sometimes be located in 35-40 feet of water on the main lake points with slabs.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are staging on points hitting Carolina rigs or rattle traps.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. On the lake crappie are fair on jigs and minnow over brush 8-16 feet of water. Black bass are fair on craw jigs and diving crankbaits in 4-10 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: As the sunshine heats up the submerged concrete and surrounding water the crappie bite should improve in these areas. The few crappie that have been caught are full of eggs, indicating the spawn is near. Crappie are fair on minnows and jigs. Bass are slow on crankbaits and spinnerbaits in deeper water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: For this reason head out rigged with the white 5/8ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab. Bass are good with fish setting up on deeper drains and tree lines in 10-20 feet of water.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie will start moving toward the creeks and coves in 8-12 feet of water on brush and structure. Bass fishing is slow but look for fish to move up and use these low lake levels to mark stumps and rocks that would normally be covered with water and fish.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: A few bass can be caught with spinnerbaits and chatterbaits around the flooded bushes and grass. Deeper bass, 8-12 feet of water, are hitting Carolina rigs and football jigs. Crappie will be slow until the water clears back up.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with fish staging up in and around the mouths of cuts and coves. Largemouth bass are good on long points with hydrilla with green pumpkin 4 inch worm, or in the grass with red rattle trap in 6-8 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught in 30 feet of water. Bass are slow in deeper water on a variety of soft plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with small jigs and minnows on timber in 15-20 feet of water on the north end of the lake. White bass are fair with flukes and slabs. Largemouth bass are fair around the docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on the main lake structure with slabs. Crappie are fair to good on brush piles and in the river on jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow and can be caught in grass 5-15 feet with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senko and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: Fish in deeper, clearer water will remain interested in the 5/8 ounce and 3/4 ounce white Bladed Hazy Eye Slab worked with a very slow, steady upward motion where fish are seen concentrated on bottom via sonar.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass have started to slow down as water temperatures have dropped. Black bass are in a pre-spawn pattern.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brady fishing report
reports.text: Target bass on first breaks just off of shallow water with Carolina rigs and rattle traps.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: As warmer temperatures return, slabs should become more effective. Crappie are slowly moving into prespawn mode.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 8 pounds are fair on scope minnows off the rocks in 8-15 feet and Hag’s bait jigs around steep banks and squarebill crankbaits in 2-14 feet. Crappie are poor on jigs and minnows in brush piles 10-15 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bryan fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught on offshore wind blown points with Carolina rigs, heavy jigs or crankbaits. Some bass are shallow on rocks with a wacky rig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: This has slowed the bass bite down, but a few can still be caught with chatterbaits and rattle traps over the grass and pad stems on the main lake. The river and bayou are very muddy with lots of current, so expect the crappie bite to be tough.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on long points with hydrilla with green pumpkin 4 inch worm, or in the grass with red rattle trap in 6-8 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and catfish are good when the wind is down on cut bait and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass should be slow this weekend. Target bass in standing timber in 8-10 feet of water with a very slow approach.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to boast on limits of eater sized channel catfish and numbers of black bass in this power plant lake. Largemouth anglers line up to get on this lake on the weekends.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Numbers of buck bass are shallow, and even some of the big gals on beds or staging on structure near beds. Crappie seem to be pretty good on the north end but with the temperature changes fish will be moving around a lot. Crappie are being caught in 13-22 feet on or near standing timber and other structures.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass have started to slow down as water temperatures have dropped.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Expect the largemouth bass bite to slow after the recent cold front. As the sunshine warms the water the bass will return to the shallows from the first drop-off.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Warm sunny days are dictating black bass movements. To fly fish for bass try game changers and craw patterns in shallow water. The Lake Fork crappie bite is really good this week if you can stand the cold weather and beat the winds. If you find a crappie and hold an artificial bait above it still enough most fish are crushing that bait.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in 15-17 feet on brush with jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass have been better on those warmer days near main lake points slowly working soft plastics. Crappie are good in the river near deeper holes and on the main lake near deep pilings and timber with small crappie jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Target fish in deep water with white slabs on a stinger hook with a small jig head with a power gulp minnow tied two feet above.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are tight to the shorelines and in structure in shallow water but with the temperatures dropping, may go deep for a bit until it warms up. Crappie are in 8 feet of water on structure and eating small jigs good.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass have backed off the bank to brush in 8-16 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass have started to slow down as water temperatures have dropped.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lavon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are in 10-20 feet of water on brush piles and deep submerged timber. Crappie are hugging the bottom so you have to let a ⅛ ounce hand tied jig touch the bottom and then slowly lift to entice a bite. Slabs and 3-4 inch flukes have been getting them. Black bass are in 1-5 feet on rocks or concrete, and in 5-10 feet of water shoreline structure. Texas rigs and bass jigs are pulling them out of 15-20 feet deep brush piles. The dam has trees and brush bluegill and crappie are mixed in. Crickets have been king as they also catch a few crappies.
reports.by: Carey Thorn, White Bass Fishing Texas

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: In the river target bass with a suspended jerkbait, dropshot and Alabama rig between dock, and the big granite boulders. Crappie are fair in 25-30 feet on brush and boulders with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good near laydowns and brush piles with jigs, Texas rigged soft plastics, lipless crankbaits and square and some days a spinner baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good, fishing the hydrilla with underspin swimbaits, lipless crankbaits and weightless senkos. Crappie are fair to good in brush piles in 15-25 feet of water with minnows and powerbait champ minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent in shallow grass with a bladed jig or a rattle trap. Crappie are slow roaming in standing timber with chartreuse jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Large numbers and quality sized bass have been boated with a deep-diving crankbait, jerkbait and the Alabama rig. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with dropshot and Carolina rigs in 15 feet of water. Crappie are good with chartreuse crappie jigs roaming around timber and brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are roaming the main lake and very skittish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair to 5 pounds on jerkbaits, Alabama rigs and deep diving crankbaits. One bass over 13 pounds reported this week. White bass are still good on main lake flats in 30-35 feet of water on slabs and spoons. Some crappie are suspended over the tops of the big pecan trees in the Turkey Bend area with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Black bass can be targeted utilizing forward facing sonar to locate bass then use a swimbait or Alabama rig to get a reaction.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: The cold weather has pushed crappie to roam deeper water. Black bass and sand bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with large swimbaits or Carolina rigs on points in 15 feet of water. Crappie are fair with primarily smaller size fish being caught with white jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 20-34 feet of water with 3/4 ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied above working best spread at least 16 inches apart. Small road runner type baits and small crappie jigs working. Crappie are fair and relating to brush 18-28 feet deep moving on and off structure and starting to roam the deep flats.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: White bass can be caught on live bait and slabs on deep water humps near creek channels 35-55 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass and small hybrids are scattered, but can sometimes be caught on slabs in 35-40 feet of water on the main lake points. No reports from anglers targeting crappie or largemouth bass.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are going to hunker down in grass and become lethargic with some fish seeking out deeper structure. Crappie are heading toward spawning areas in 2-3 feet of water on flats, grass and cypress trees.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow off the concrete at the pump house, and near docks. Bass are slow on crankbaits and spinnerbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: Fish in deeper, clearer water will remain interested in the 5/8 ounce and 3/4 ounce white Bladed Hazy Eye Slab worked with a very slow, steady upward motion where fish are seen concentrated on bottom via sonar.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: The crappie bite is also slow under bridges and deep timber in 18-25 feet. The largemouth bite has been slow, but the big warm-up coming next week will change this overnight.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on deep structure and brush in 18-25 feet of water near creeks and coves. Bass fishing is slow with the drop in lake levels and water temperature. Fish creeks and stumps looking for the gizzard shad this time of year for bigger bass to be feeding.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good when the weather warms, then back to tough on the colder days.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Good numbers of bass in 5-15 feet and 30-40 feet of water on ledges with brush hogs, medium to large creature baits, medium to deep crankbaits, squarebill crankbaits and jerkbaits. Largemouth bass are good on long points with hydrilla with green pumpkin 4 inch worm, or in the grass with red rattle trap in 6-8 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow but chasing shad.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on the main lake structure on slabs. Crappie are fair to good on brush piles and in the river on jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie continue to be good in 14-30 feet of water on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair on jigs, flatheads good on live bait. Bass are in a prespawn mode with quality fish and limits possible. Bass are best utilizing forward facing sonar using jighead minnow presentations, Texas rigged plastics and jerkbaits. Report by Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Arlington fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with creature baits, jigs and moving baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Athens fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow and can be caught in grass 8-15 feet with Texas rig worms, wacky rig senkos and lipless crankbaits. Crappie are slow on small jigs over deep brush 25 feet. Report by Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide.
reports.by: Reagan Nelson, Lake Athens Bass Guide

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is improving rapidly with a good shallow bite going on right now. The water temperature in some of the creeks is in the low 60s, so anticipate bass to spawn within the next month.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake B.A. Steinhagen fishing report
reports.text: Bass can be caught with Carolina rigged plastics, crankbaits and rattle traps. Crappie are fair with jigs or minnows in flooded timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good continuing to push shallower to stage for the spawn. Black bass are in pre-spawn pattern.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Expect the crappie to become stationary to reserve energy. If this happens crappie will feed on the shad and follow the fish deep to feed. Crappie are good in 20-60 feet of water on timber in the creek channels. The primary species being caught is black crappie.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Hybrids and Sand Bass are fair on soft plastics and slabs. Crappie are in prespawn mode. Largemouth bass are also in pre-spawn mode.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 3 pounds are slow on jigs around bait and squarebill crankbaits in 2-4 feet of water. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows in brush piles 10-15 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: Bass are spawning in shallow water due to the combination of the full moon and the water temperature. Cast Alabama rigs, rattle traps or crankbaits in the river and bayou near the spawning flats, if the weather becomes very cold bass will stack up off spawning flats.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Canyon Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good for numbers.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Coleto Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 2-6 feet of water in the reeds and hardwood timber with Watermelon candy red plastics.
reports.by: Scott Springer, Fish Choke Canyon Lake

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Comanche Creek continues to boast numbers of largemouth bass and channel catfish. Largemouth bass are good to 7 pounds on soft plastics fished near channel breaks.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass have been plentiful up shallow and on near bed structure. Crappie have been on the move, but slow to bite. Crappie are being caught in 13-22 feet on or near standing timber and other structures. Target fish in 16-24 feet on flats and drop-offs trolling or using slabs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cypress Springs fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good continuing to push shallower to stage for the spawn.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow. Bass are good for quality but not for numbers in 8-15 feet of water with plastics and crankbaits. Bass are good in the rocks with medium to shallow running crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good in shallow water with shaky heads, Carolina rigs, chatterbaits and rattle traps. Most bass are pushing shallow to spawn.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in 3-5 feet of water with squarebill crankbaits, and chatterbaits. Warm sunny days are dictating black bass movements. To fly fish for bass try game changers and craw patterns in shallow water. The Lake Fork crappie bite is really good this week if you can stand the cold weather and beat the winds. If you find a crappie and hold an artificial bait above it still enough most fish are crushing that bait.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ft. Phantom Hill fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with catches up to 7 pounds possible on wacky rig senkos targeting shallow rocks, points and flats. Crappie are good at the intake, but primarily smaller size catches.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Fishing is still a little slow for bass. Crappie are good in deeper water near brush in 17 feet on minows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Sand bass are good on roadrunners and small jigs and slab combinations. Largemouth bass are good near main lake points and in deeper holes up river with soft plastics and crankbaits. Crappie action is good with small jigs on submerged structures from Water’s Edge to Stockton Bend.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair up river on jigs fished around cover. Crappie are moving shallow to the backs of coves when the water warms up after three warm nights.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are grouped up tight around structures in the rivers and around dogs, eating grubs and small worms. Sometimes bass are higher in the water column. Crappie are tight to structure and 14-20 feet of water, eating small hand ties, jigs, and minnows.
reports.by: Captain Zackary Scott, Zack Attack Fishing

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Houston County fishing report
reports.text: Crappie can be caught with minnows and jigs. Bass can be caught on crankbaits and Carolina rigged plastics.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass are biting shallow on soft plastics, rattle traps, and chatterbaits. Some bass are schooled up in deep water hitting crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O' the Pines fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good continuing to push shallower to stage for the spawn.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: The Colorado River is producing bass along the rocks with Alabama rigs. Crappie are good in 25-30 feet on brush and boulders with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good near laydowns and brush piles with jigs, Texas rigged soft plastics, lipless crankbaits and square and some days a spinner baits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair to good on deep flats and in river channels in 42-64 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 4-38 feet of water on brush piles, bridge pilings, and submerged cover near a drop-off ledge with minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Livingston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are going to be shallow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The bass bite has improved on most areas of the lake. Crappie fishing has improved in 20-25 feet of water on brush piles and standing timber using minnows and larger jigs like a 3 inch powerbait champ minnow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent in 15-18 feet of water on Carolina rigs deep diving crankbaits. Crappie are fair with nice fish 13.5-16 inches cruising around standing timber.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Large numbers of quality bass are possible with a deep-diving crankbait, jerkbaits and Alabama rig. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are excellent with a Carolina rigged creature bait on secondary points. Crappie are excellent with white or chartreuse crappie jigs roaming around timber and brush piles.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slowly staging shallow for the spawn. Crappie are in 6-8 feet of water off the docks and brushier areas hitting minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good with fish to 7 pound possible in 8-18 feet along brush lines on main Lake points and drains with shad patterned jerkbaits, umbrella rigs, swim jigs and some chatterbaits. Some crappie are still deep in main Lake trees around Ranger Cove and in front of Elm Creek where it dumps into The Colorado River. Crappie are suspended in 25 feet hitting primarily minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palestine fishing report
reports.text: Before the cold front bass and crappie were spawning along the banks. Target bass secondary points and ditches near spawning grounds with a slow approach worm, jig or brush hog. Crappie can be found 4-30 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are plentiful schooling in deep water. Crappie will start to transition to spawning beds as the water temperature continues to increase. Black bass are slow.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on Alabama rigs and swimbaits in 12-15 feet of water. Crappie are slow with live minnows.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Possum Kingdom fishing report
reports.text: Bass slow but will bite when located. Bass biting from deep to shallow depths following shad movement. Report by JK Outdoors Bass Fishing Guide.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Hubbard fishing report
reports.text: Look for big bait balls in 20-34 feet of water with 3/4 ounce slabs with 2 jigs tied above working best spread at least 16 inches apart. Small roadrunner type baits and small crappie jigs are working. Crappie are fair on minnows related to brush in 18-28 feet of water. Crappie are moving on and off structure and starting to roam the deep flats.
reports.by: John Varner, John Varner's Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: White bass and small hybrids can be located in 35-40 feet of water on the Windsock Point and caught on slabs.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass are starting to spawn in the creek channels and buck brush. With the forecasted cold front, expect bass to hunker down in grass and become lethargic with some fish seeking out deeper structure. Crappie are heading toward spawning areas in 2-3 feet of water on flats, grass and cypress trees.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Somerville fishing report
reports.text: At Somerville marina the crappie bite is fair, bluegill are fair on crickets and worms, and catfish are fair on minnows and punch bait. On the lake crappie are fair on jigs and minnow over brush 8-16 feet of water. Black bass are fair moving plastics in 6-12 feet of water.
reports.by: Weldon Kirk, Fish Tales Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are fair with some activity in the crappie house. Bass are fair with some catches near the crappie house.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tawakoni fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have remained steady on bridge pilings in 15-20 feet with jigs outfishing minnows. Largemouth bass are good last week as the shallows warmed up.
reports.by: Captain Michael Littlejohn, Lake Tawakoni Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: As water temperatures start to fall, look for crappie in deeper water on brush and structure in 18-25 feet of water. Bass are hitting soft plastics and slow moving baits off the banks in 8-12 feet of water as fish are pulled to deeper water due to falling water temperature and lake levels.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Before the rain bass were good shallow with fish up to 6-7 pounds caught on spinnerbaits, chatterbaits and squarebill crankbaits. Crappie bite was good in the creeks with live bait in 5-10 feet of water, but expect the rain to slow the bite down.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Good numbers of bass in 5-15 feet and 30-40 feet of water on ledges with brush hogs, medium to large creature baits, medium to deep crankbaits, squarebill crankbaits and jerkbaits. Bass fishing has been best on the lower end hydrilla and grass with jerkbaits and chatterbaits, and Alabama rig.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow but moving back shallow. Crappie are starting to spawn in 8 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Waco fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are good up to 7 pounds on main river channels leading into the creeks and coves. Crappie are slow with fish scattered throughout the lake with live minnows or red jigheads. Report by Greg Culverhouse, Crappie King.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Alan Henry fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 14-30 feet of water on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Amistad fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are in 20 feet of water on soft plastics. Crappie are good on minnows and jigs. Cold weather has driven bass to quick drop areas from 15-45 feet of water. Report by Kurt Dove, Pro Bass Guide.
reports.by: Shon Riley, Lake Amistad Fishing Guides

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Austin fishing report
reports.text: Large groups of bass are in 8-12 feet of water on grass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Belton fishing report
reports.text: The white, 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab with stinger hook has been a solid bet since late November and continued producing fish this week. A slow-smoking tactic worked best wherein the slab is slowly reeled upwards to be followed by bottom-hugging fish, or is slowly reeled upwards past suspended fish.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bob Sandlin fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have also been suspended on deep vertical cover in 15-25 feet and the biggest crappie in the school will bite a damiki rig. Black bass are beginning their pre-spawn.
reports.by: Blake Doughtie, Lake Country Lunkers Lures and Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bois d'Arc fishing report
reports.text: Bass continue to be slow while water temperatures are 45-48 degrees, but a few places are 50 degrees in the timber. Expect the crappie to become stationary to reserve energy. If this happens crappie will feed on the shad and follow the fish deep to feed. Crappie are good in 20-60 feet of water on timber in the creek channels. The primary species being caught is black crappie.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Braunig fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the weeds on plastic worms.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Bridgeport fishing report
reports.text: Hybrids and sand bass are fair on slabs and deadstick plastic baits. Largemouth bass are fair on swimbaits and jig and pig combinations.
reports.by: Keith Bunch, Lake Bridgeport Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Brownwood fishing report
reports.text: Black bass to 5 pounds are poor on jigs around bait balls in open water scoping and squarebill crankbaits in 2-4 feet. Crappie are slow on jigs and minnows in brush piles 15-20 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Buchanan fishing report
reports.text: Bass are shallow anywhere near balls of bait. Crappie are good in 10-15 feet of water over brush and trees. Crappie are fair on chartreuse jigs in 15-20 feet of water. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Caddo fishing report
reports.text: In a few weeks the bass pattern will change when fish move to trees.
reports.by: Vince Richards, Caddo Lake Fishing & Fellowship

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Calaveras fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good in the weeds on plastic worms and crawfish.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Cisco fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are hit-or-miss with minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Comanche Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are active and can be caught on crankbaits and soft plastics. Reports continue to say that 30-50 fish days are possible for bass.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Conroe fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good feeding on shad schools early in the morning then moving offshore as the day progresses. Crappie are being caught in 13-22 feet on or near standing timber and other structures.
reports.by: Roy Crush IV and Bradley Doyle, Bradley’s Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Eagle Mountain fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on main lake structure on slabs and in mid depths on chartreuse and white cocahoes. Crappie are fair in open water roaming patterns and in mid depths and main lake structure on jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Falcon fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow. Bass are good for quality but not for numbers in 8-15 feet of water with plastics and crankbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fayette fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good with some big fish being caught in shallow water with shaky heads, Carolina rigs, chatterbaits and rattle traps. Bass are not bunching up in deep water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Fork fishing report
reports.text: Rising water and warm sunny days will kick off the pre-spawn bite for larger male bass in 5-8 feet of water. The Lake Fork crappie bite is improving daily after the huge cold snap and loads of water the lake received the last few weeks.
reports.by: Marc Mitchell, Lake Fork Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Graham fishing report
reports.text: Fishing is still a little slow for bass. Crappie are good in deeper water near brush in 17 feet on minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granbury fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass continue to be good in numbers on soft plastics especially on those warmer days. Main lake points and the river above Granbury are boasting on the largemouth bass catches. Crappie are fair to good on small jigs on deeper timber and bridge piling. Lots of crappie are being caught in the river near Tin Top as well.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Granger fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are fair up river on grubs and in line spinners. Crappie are fair on jigs and minnows fished up river and in Willis Creek.
reports.by: Tommy Tidwell, Tommy Tidwell’s Granger Lake Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Grapevine fishing report
reports.text: Utilize a thumper and white slabs on a stinger hook with a small jig head with a power gulp minnow tied two feet above.
reports.by: Omar Cotter, Luck O’the Irish Fishing Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Jacksonville fishing report
reports.text: Bass were biting on soft plastics, crankbaits and swimbaits on brush piles in 10-18 feet.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Joe Pool Lake fishing report
reports.text: It is a great time to target a big largemouth bass. Bass will travel to shallow water so look for the first major piece of structure on the travel route. Crappie can be found schooled up on deep brush piles or flooded timber.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake LBJ fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good in 25-30 feet on brush and boulders with minnows. Report by Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service. Bass are good near laydowns and brush piles with jigs and Texas rigged soft plastics, lipless crankbaits and square and some days a spinner baits.
reports.by: Jess Rotherham, Texas Crappie Fishing Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Lewisville fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on deep flats and in river channels in 42-64 feet of water with jigs, slabs, and live bait. Crappie are fair in 4-38 feet of water on brush piles, bridge pilings, and submerged cover near a drop-off ledge with minnows and jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Limestone fishing report
reports.text: Catfish crappie and largemouth bass are suspended this week. Crappie are in 10-18 feet on brush, standing timber and power line columns with minnows. A lot of crappie are roaming the creek channels getting ready to push to the creeks for the spawn. Largemouth bass are in 8 feet of water On docks, rocks and bulkheads with Texas rigs and chatterbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Martin Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on most of the lake now. Crappie are good in the pipeline area in 10-15 feet around fallen timber on minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Meredith fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are good on artificial grubs and minnows in Sanford Yake Cove and Bugbee. No reports of crappie this week.
reports.by: Dave Wright, Wright-On Bait, Tackle and Watercraft Rental

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nacogdoches fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are fair on shallow bladed jigs, rattle traps in 1-6 feet in grassy areas on the north end. Crappie are good on chartreuse jigs roaming timber.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Naconiche fishing report
reports.text: Bass are mostly hovering just off the bottom, so a drop-shot has been working pretty well. Crappie population is good. Largemouth bass are good in 20 feet of water with small minnow baits and large glide baits. Crappie are excellent with white and chartreuse jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Navarro Mills fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slowly staging shallow for the spawn. Crappie are in 6-8 feet of water off the docks and brushier areas jigs or minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake O.H. Ivie fishing report
reports.text: Black bass are slow to fair with a few fish ranging from 8-11 pounds caught this last week. Some bass are in 10-15 feet of water on brush edges, with some fish as deep as 35 feet. Crappie are fair suspended 20-30 feet down over deep trees in 40-50 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Oak Creek Lake fishing report
reports.text: The black bass bite has improved with reports of fish caught over 12 pounds and many reports of 8-10 pound catches. The most popular method currently is using forward facing sonar to locate bass and use a swimbait or Alabama rig to get a reaction. Reports of 11 inch crappie being caught off brush piles with small jigs and swimbaits.
reports.by: Bronte Guns and Tackle Pro Staff

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Palo Pinto fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are very good on jigs and minnows.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Pinkston fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass are excellent in 20-30 feet with forward facing sonar on small minnow baits and large glide baits. Crappie are slow with 1/16 ounce white crappie jigs.
reports.by: Cal Cameron, Cal’s ETX Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Ray Roberts fishing report
reports.text: White bass are good on live bait and slabs in 35-55 feet of water on deep water humps near creek channels.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Richland Chambers fishing report
reports.text: Suspended fish can be caught with a slab and jig combination fished in 30-40 feet of water off main lake points and Pelican Island. A young angler scouting for an upcoming High School Bass Tournament caught a 13.64 pound bass on Sunday, January 26. Last time a largemouth bass of this size was caught was in 2008, and the record is 14.25 pounds was caught in 1995.
reports.by: Royce Simmons, Gone Fishin' Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sam Rayburn fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has improved in the creeks as fish transition to spawning areas. Crappie are in the creek channels and river.
reports.by: Captain Lynn Atkinson, Reel Um N Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stamford fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good with some activity in the crappie house. Bass are good with some catches near the crappie house. If it’s a warm rain it may trigger the bass to transition shallow to feed

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Stillhouse fishing report
reports.text: The white, 5/8 ounce Bladed Hazy Eye Slab with stinger hook has been a solid bet since late November and continued producing fish this week. A slow-smoking tactic worked best wherein the slab is slowly reeled upwards to be followed by bottom-hugging fish, or is slowly reeled upwards past suspended fish -- regardless, once fish begin following, you must keep moving the bait to get bit.
reports.by: Bob Maindelle, Holding the Line Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Texoma fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are on brush and structure in 18–25 feet of water, but target shallower water on warmer days as fish start to move toward creeks and coves on the lake. To target bass, focus on rocks and structures that hold baitfish in warmer water.
reports.by: Jacob Orr, Lake Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Toledo Bend fishing report
reports.text: Bass are good on spinnerbaits and chatterbaits from 2-4 feet around flooded bushes, lipless baits are good over the top of grass or hay grass in 4-7 feet, Texas and Carolina rigged lizards are good on main lake points from 12-18 feet. No crappie report, but expect this bite to begin any day.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Travis fishing report
reports.text: Good numbers of bass in 5-15 feet and 30-40 feet of water on ledges with brush hogs, medium to large creature baits, medium to deep crankbaits, squarbill crankbaits and jerkbaits.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Twin Buttes fishing report
reports.text: Crappie and white bass are slow.
reports.by: Captain Michael Peterson, 4 Reel Fun Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Tyler fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow on crankbaits and trick worms. Crappie are slow on minnows in 25-30 feet of water.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: White River fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good deadsticking jigs in 10-17 feet of water around brush.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Whitney fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good on small jigs and minnows in timber in 15-20 feet on the north end of the lake. White bass fishing is fair, some are being caught on flukes and slabs. Largemouth bass fishing is fair around the docks.
reports.by: Captain Cory Vinson, Guaranteed Guide Service

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Worth fishing report
reports.text: White bass are fair on main lake structure on slabs. Crappie are fair to good on brush piles and in the river on jigs.

reports.source: Texas Parks and Wildlife weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Wright Patman fishing report
reports.text: Bass are slow. Crappie are staged on brush in 8-12 feet but the fish are not biting.
